name: Shorshe Ilish
subtitle: Hilsa poached in a raw mustard paste, the dish Bengal argues about most

ingredients.note: any oily river fish; do not skin it

prepNotes: Mustard turns bitter if the paste is ground hot or too long. Soak the seeds, add a green chilli and a pinch of salt, and grind in short bursts.
Hilsa is full of fine bones and is eaten carefully rather than filleted. Do not substitute a boneless fillet and expect the same dish.

steps.text: Soak the mustard seeds 20 minutes in warm water, then grind with 2 green chillies and a pinch of salt to a smooth paste. Strain if you want it silky.
steps.tip: Short bursts. Overgrinding is what makes mustard bitter.

steps.text: Rub the fish with turmeric and salt and rest 10 minutes.
Heat the mustard oil until it just smokes, then take it off the heat for a moment. This removes the raw pungency.
Return to low heat, add the nigella, then the mustard paste thinned with half a cup of water, the remaining chillies and salt. Simmer 3 minutes.
steps.tip: Do not brown the paste; this is a raw mustard sauce, not a bhuna.

steps.text: Slide in the fish in a single layer, spoon the sauce over, cover and cook 8 minutes. Do not stir, shake the pan.
Finish with a tablespoon of raw mustard oil poured over, and rest 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

storage: Eat the same day. Hilsa firms unpleasantly on reheating and mustard sauces turn bitter overnight. Do not freeze.
